items.body:
`netaddr.fbsocket.inet_ntoa` requires `packed_ip` to be a `str` (line 19) and then unpacks it with `struct.unpack('4B', ...)`, which needs bytes. On Python 3 no value passes both, so every IPv4 conversion fails, including the module's own `inet_pton` output:

```python
>>> from netaddr import fbsocket
>>> fbsocket.inet_ntop(fbsocket.AF_INET, b'\x01\x02\x03\x04')
TypeError: string type expected, not <class 'bytes'>
>>> fbsocket.inet_ntop(fbsocket.AF_INET, fbsocket.inet_pton(fbsocket.AF_INET, '1.2.3.4'))
TypeError: string type expected, not <class 'bytes'>
>>> fbsocket.inet_ntop(fbsocket.AF_INET6, fbsocket.inet_pton(fbsocket.AF_INET6, '::ffff:1.2.3.4'))
TypeError: string type expected, not <class 'bytes'>
```

The module is a fallback for the `socket` module, whose `inet_ntoa` and `inet_ntop` take bytes. The IPv6 branch of `inet_ntop` already checks for `bytes` (line 82), so the `str` check in `inet_ntoa` looks like a Python 2 leftover. IPv6 addresses with an embedded IPv4 part fail too, as shown above.

Found by differential testing against IPy's `IPint.strCompressed`.
Versions: netaddr 1.3.0, Python 3.12.
items.title: fbsocket.inet_ntoa and inet_ntop raise TypeError for every IPv4 address on Python 3

items.body:
## Summary

`IPAddress.is_loopback()`, `is_link_local()`, `is_ipv4_private_use()`, and `is_global()` never look through the IPv4-mapped form. Every `::ffff:a.b.c.d` address is classified as `reserved` regardless of what the embedded IPv4 address actually is:

```python
import netaddr, ipaddress

netaddr.IPAddress('::ffff:127.0.0.1').is_loopback()          # False
ipaddress.ip_address('::ffff:127.0.0.1').is_loopback         # True  (stdlib looks through)

netaddr.IPAddress('::ffff:169.254.169.254').is_link_local()  # False
ipaddress.ip_address('::ffff:169.254.169.254').is_link_local # True

netaddr.IPAddress('::ffff:8.8.8.8').is_global()              # False
ipaddress.ip_address('::ffff:8.8.8.8').is_global             # True
```

The socket layer sides with stdlib. Verified live: a listener bound to `127.0.0.1` accepts a connection made to `::ffff:127.0.0.1` — the kernel's dual-stack routes the v4-mapped form to the embedded IPv4 address.

## Why this matters

SSRF filters are commonly written as an enumeration of bad targets:

```python
ip = netaddr.IPAddress(host)
if ip.is_loopback() or ip.is_link_local():   # block localhost & cloud metadata
    reject()
```

That filter blocks `127.0.0.1` and `169.254.169.254` but **misses `::ffff:127.0.0.1` and `::ffff:169.254.169.254`**, which the network stack treats as the same endpoints. (Filters written as `if not ip.is_global(): reject()` fail closed here — though they also wrongly block legitimate v4-mapped globals like `::ffff:8.8.8.8`.)

For context, both netaddr and stdlib are additionally blind to NAT64 (`64:ff9b::127.0.0.1`) and 6to4 (`2002:7f00:1::`) embeddings of loopback — that's a wider industry gap, not what I'm reporting here. The netaddr-specific issue is the v4-mapped form, which stdlib handles and netaddr does not.

## Suggested fix

In each predicate, when `is_ipv4_mapped()` is true, delegate to the embedded IPv4 address's predicate (e.g. `is_loopback()` returns `self.ipv4().is_loopback()` for mapped forms). Happy to send a PR with tests if you'd take it.

Checked the tracker for prior reports of this and found none. Found via differential testing of netaddr against Python's stdlib `ipaddress` over the IANA special-registry space (30,000 generated addresses plus a curated edge battery), produced by AI agents working under my direction; analysis, socket-level verification, and this report were run and reviewed by me.
items.title: Security predicates don't look through IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (::ffff:a.b.c.d)

items.body:
```python
import netaddr

ip = netaddr.IPAddress('fec0::1')
print(ip.info)
print(ip.is_reserved())
```

```
{'IPv6': [{'allocation': 'Reserved by IETF',
 'prefix': 'fec0::/10',
 'reference': 'rfc3879'}]}
False
```

While ULAs have superseded site-local prefixes, the prefix is [still reserved by IANA](https://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv6-address-space/ipv6-address-space.xhtml).
Thus `.is_reserved()` should report `True`.

The docstring for `.is_reserved` mentions only [RFC 3330](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3330) (which has been obsoleted by [5735](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5735), which is not even mentioned in the docstring) and [RFC 3171](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3171) (which, also, has been obsoleted by [5771](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5771) - no mention either), but both of these references are only for IPv4.

I'd recommend updating wherever these reservation states are being tracked.
Current data is [here](https://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv4-address-space/ipv4-address-space.xml) for IPv4 and [here](https://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv6-address-space/ipv6-address-space.xml) for IPv6.
Should be a breeze to update; both can be fetched as XML.
